item.title: Salah scores twice to create record as Egypt crush Malawi
item.description: Mohamed Salah celebrates after scoring for Egypt in a penalty shootout against Australia during the 2026 World Cup (Kevin C. Cox) Mohamed Salah scored twice as Egypt routed Malawi 5-0 in an Africa Cup of Nations qualifier on Friday to become the leading all-time scorer for his country with 70 goals. The 34-year-old former Liverpool star left it late in Cairo to overtake Hossam Hassan, scoring with a far-post header on 84 minutes and from a penalty five minutes into added time. Hassan was fired as Egypt coach last week and replacement Ali Maher made a perfect start with goals from Nasser Maher, Omar Marmoush and Mohamed Hany building a 3-0 lead by half-time. Egypt have seven points in Group B after three matches, three more than Angola, who host South Sudan on Saturday. Achraf Hakimi, favourite to win a second successive African Footballer of the Year award next month, also bagged a brace as Group A pacesetters Morocco crushed Niger 5-1 in Casablanca. Substitute Tolu Arokodaro scored twice within eight minutes as Nigeria beat Tanzania 3-1 in Uyo to get their campaign back on track. Tunisia suffered a shock home 2-0 loss to Libya and Kenya scored in the final minute to snatch a surprise 2-2 draw away to South Africa. Alhassan Yusuf put Nigeria ahead after just 103 seconds and Alphonce Msanga equalised on 32 minutes following a rare Tanzanian attack. Arokodaro, scorer of six goals in his last five matches for Ajax Amsterdam, came off the bench for the second half and quickly made an impact. His near-post back heel off a low cross put Nigeria ahead a second time after 52 minutes and as the match reached the hour mark, he struck again, with a close-range shot. An ultimately comfortable victory lifted the Super Eagles to six points after three rounds in Group L, one point behind Guinea-Bissau, who drew 1-1 with Madagascar on Thursday. - Nigeria boost - Although bottom of the table with just one point, Tanzania are guaranteed a place at the 2027 AFCON as co-hosts with Kenya and Uganda. That means Guinea-Bissau, Nigeria and Madagascar must fight for one place at the 24-nation tournament, the first to be staged in east Africa since Ethiopia were the 1976 hosts. Nigeria were in trouble after a 3-0 hammering in Guinea-Bissau two months ago, but now have a clear path to a tournament they have won three times. Away wins over Tanzania, on Tuesday, and Madagascar in March, and a home win over Guinea-Bissau, also in March, will assure qualification. Tunisia are in Group H, which includes co-hosts and automatic qualifiers Uganda, and their record of reaching every AFCON tournament since 1994 is in peril. A 2-0 defeat at home to neighbours Libya leaves them bottom of the table with just two points, and a venue switch two months ago means their remaining three fixtures are all away. item.title: Haslem Sets The Tone For Giannis And Bam After Rough Start
item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Miami Heat are sitting at 5-6, a record that makes no sense for a team that traded the world to get Giannis Antetokounmpo. The Greek Freak is putting up big numbers, but the losses keep piling up. That kind of pressure usually makes stars question their choices. Instead, Heat legend Udonis Haslem stepped in to set the record straight for his new teammate. This week, Antetokounmpo was addressed directly by Haslem, the vice president of basketball development. The 46-year-old veteran told the star that he cannot pick and choose when the hard times happen. According to HITC , Haslem said: “I told Giannis today: ‘Listen, you don’t get to pick and choose when the adversity hits. You just pick and choose how you respond.'” This message cuts through the noise and tells the team exactly what they need to hear right now. Adversity Hits Early or Late Haslem knows this league better than most, having spent 20 years in a Heat uniform. He explained that bad stretches come for everyone, just at different times. Some teams face trouble at the start, while others get hit in the middle or at the end. The Heat are dealing with it right now, and Haslem sees that as a blessing in disguise. He told Antetokounmpo that getting the pain out of the way early is the better option than saving it for the end of the season. The advice is simple but hard to follow. You cannot change the schedule or the opponents, but you can control your reaction. Haslem noted that if a player gets to choose, they should choose to face the hard stuff now. This approach forces the team to grow faster instead of waiting for a crisis later. Bam Must Play His Own Game While Giannis gets advice on mindset, center Bam Adebayo gets a reality check on his style. Haslem told Adebayo to stop trying to be someone else. The veteran captain made it clear that Adebayo has the talent to score 30 points a night, but he needs to do it his way. According to HITC, Haslem said: “You’re an effort and energy guy, that has All Star talent. You’re not Joel Embiid.” Haslem pointed out that Embiid can score from a kneeling position, but Adebayo’s path to those numbers requires constant motion and intensity. The goal is not to copy a different player’s moves but to use his own unique strengths to dominate. Before retiring, a man who previously shared a locker room with Adebayo made these comments. Haslem has watched Bam grow into a leader and knows exactly what he brings to the floor. The Heat need both stars to buy into these roles to fix their defensive rating, which currently sits as the fifth-worst in the league. The team faces a long road to fix their defense, but the leadership is finally speaking up.

item.title: France hold on for thrilling Nations Championship win over South Africa
item.description: France beat South Africa for only the second time in their last 11 Tests dating back to 2009 (FRANCK FIFE) France pulled off a stunning and nervy 21-19 victory over world champions South Africa in the Nations Championship on Friday. A brilliant first-half display and gutsy second-half showing amid a flood of cards handed Les Bleus only their second win over the Springboks in their last 11 Tests. Captain Antoine Dupont was named man of the match in a pulsating encounter that contrasted the running invention of the French with South Africa's bludgeoning force. And in the end, the only difference was a missed conversion by Springboks replacement fly-half Manie Libbok. France, though, were almost undone by wayward kicking, especially from half-back Maxime Lucu. The hosts' backs sparkled in the first half with wings Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang and Louis Bielle-Biarrey, and full-back Theo Attissogbe scoring a try each in a scintillating first half. But South Africa's brute force and forward power kept them in touch, scoring two catch-and-drive tries. Tries from hookers Jan-Hendrik Wessels and Malcolm Marx, and a close-range effort from replacement scrum-half Cobus Reinach, helped them storm back from a 21-7 half-time deficit, but it was not enough. It was South Africa's first defeat in the tournament and hands the initiative to New Zealand in the southern hemisphere pool. France, though, ensured that they will maintain their lead in the northern hemisphere section ahead of next weekend's clash against Argentina, keeping them in pole position to reach the final at Twickenham in two weeks' time. - Electrifying - The build-up to the match had been peppered with mind games. Having been named on the team sheet at fly-half, Dupont played at scrum-half with Lucu outside him. And an hour before kick-off, South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus swapped his entire starting front row with the three players initially named on the bench. France blew two early chances to open the scoring as Lucu kicked for the corner instead of the posts. The first time he fluffed his lines and South Africa won a penalty at the subsequent scrum. And the second time, the Springboks stole the line-out. But things turned in France's favour on 13 minutes as Bok lock Lood de Jager saw yellow for a high tackle on Lucu. Grandidier-Nkanang made them pay after 15 phases of play by diving over in the corner, with Lucu converting. And before De Jager returned, Attissogbe pounced on a lucky ricochet off Kalvin Gourgue's head to score a second. South Africa hit back on the half-hour mark with a classic tactic. Their scrum won a penalty, which they kicked to the corner before mauling hooker Wessels over for the try. But France hit back immediately as hooker Peato Mauvaka, who was a last-minute replacement for Julien Marchand, broke from a ruck and Dupont sent in a delectable grubber for the electrifying Bielle-Biarrey to notch his 30th try in 29 Tests. item.title: Willis On IR: Dolphins Coach Shuts Down Any QB Debate For Now
item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Dolphins made their move on Tuesday by placing starting quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve. Placing starting quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve comes after an MRI on Monday showed his core muscle injury had gotten worse. Coach Jeff Hafley confirmed the team’s stance on Wednesday, stating there will be no quarterback controversy while backup Kyle McCord takes over. The coaching staff wants Willis to rest so he can return healthy, but the immediate path forward belongs to McCord. Hafley explained that he watched Willis struggle to move during the loss to Detroit in Week 9. “You look back at Malik and you watch him in that last game and you could see it,” Hafley said Wednesday, according to WPBF . He noted that Willis was gritting through the pain but could not move like he did earlier in the year. The team signed Willis to a three-year, $67.5 million deal in March, yet his health remains the biggest question mark for the franchise. McCord Takes The Reins Kyle McCord is now the man under center for the upcoming matchup against the Indianapolis Colts. This summer, McCord was obtained by the Dolphins from the Green Bay Packers in exchange for a future sixth-round pick. He has not taken a regular-season snap for Miami yet, but he is ready to compete. “I pride myself on just being the ultimate competitor out there on the field,” McCord said Wednesday, according to Sports Illustrated . He believes his speed in processing information and accuracy will help him succeed in his first NFL start. Hafley was clear that he sees no debate about who starts if Willis does not return soon. “You guys will ask me,” Hafley said, “yes, he’ll be the starting quarterback if he returns.” The coach added that the team needs to get through the next four weeks to see how many games remain in the season. “I think you get through these four weeks, so it would leave four or five games left, and we’ll see,” Hafley said. This timeline will determine if the team can bring Willis back before the season ends. A Tough Road Ahead In his initial eight starts, Willis has thrown six touchdowns and six interceptions while completing 58.2% of passes for 1,396 yards. He showed the arm talent and mobility that brought him to Miami, but his decision-making has been inconsistent. The loss to the Lions on Sunday, Nov. 8, was ugly, with Willis throwing an interception and recording just 128 passing yards. His groin tightness during that game signaled the injury was becoming a major issue. The Dolphins face a difficult stretch without their planned franchise quarterback. They will play the Colts on Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1 p.m. ET at Lucas Oil Stadium.

item.title: Zach LaVine Wants Giannis, Heat Eye Free Agents After Slow Start
item.description: Credit: Sergio Estrada-Imagn Images The Miami Heat face a tough reality just three weeks into the 2026-27 season. They sit at 5-6 and need wins against weak teams to stay near .500. Sacramento Kings guard Zach LaVine reportedly wants to play alongside Giannis Antetokounmpo in Miami. The Heat look for immediate help to fix their roster holes. Heat insiders say the team is desperate for better perimeter depth. They have tried to fill gaps with mid-level exceptions, but the results are mixed. Adding a high-volume scorer like LaVine would change the offense. He is averaging 22.3 points per game this season. LaVine Could Fix the Backcourt LaVine is 31 years old and has only four postseason games in his career. He might be looking for a new challenge to boost his resume. According to Heavy.com , NBA insider Jake Fischer reported that Miami is a spot that LaVine would “like to go to.” The Heat cleared their roster to get Giannis, leaving them thin on the wings. They added Klay Thompson and Tim Hardaway Jr., but the depth is still shaky. Among league guards, LaVine previously ranked as one of the top scorers. His numbers have dipped, but his touch remains sharp. He played a career-low 25 games in 2023-24 due to injuries. His scoring ability next to Antetokounmpo would force defenses to choose between two threats. Giannis Is Staying Put While the Heat hunt for new pieces, the future of their star remains uncertain. ESPN front office insider Bobby Marks says Giannis will sign a new deal soon. “Giannis will extend with them either in January or sign a new deal this summer,” Marks said, according to BasketNews.com . He added, “So, it’s not like we’re putting, you know, he’s going to be looking at other things, right?” Giannis is in year two of his fully guaranteed three-year, $175 million max deal. He can choose to keep a player option worth $62.8 million for the 2027-28 campaign. Beginning Jan. 6, a four-year, $275 million extension becomes available for him to sign. If he waits until summer 2027, he could get a five-year deal worth $357 million. The Heat have secured their cornerstone, but the supporting cast needs work. Other Options on the Table The Heat are not just looking at LaVine. They are also considering veteran free agents Kevin Porter Jr. and Gabe Vincent. Porter Jr. offers versatility and could play multiple positions off the bench. Vincent has history with the team and helped them reach the NBA Finals in 2020 and 2023. The Heat have a game against the Cavaliers on Friday. They need to win that matchup to build momentum. The team is 5-2 in their last seven games, but they beat weak opponents.

item.title: Davion Mitchell Is The One Heat Player They Can’t Lose
item.description: Credit: David Kirouac-Imagn Images The Miami Heat cannot afford to lose Davion Mitchell. He has become the engine that keeps this team moving forward. Without his steady hand and elite defense, the roster falls apart fast. The stats prove he is the most vital piece on the court right now. Mitchell is playing as much as much as Bam or Giannis on the team. He has averaged 35.8 minutes per game, which tops the entire roster. His scoring numbers are strong too, with 16.5 points and 8 assists per contest. According to Sports Illustrated , he shoots 49.6 percent from the field and 40.3 percent from three-point range. Those splits are rare and show he does not force bad shots. The Bench Struggles Are Real While Mitchell thrives, Tim Hardaway Jr. is stuck in a deep hole. Hardaway started the season with high hopes but has failed to deliver. He is scoring only 4.3 points per game and shooting under 30 percent from the floor. His defense has been a major problem as well. Coach Erik Spoelstra has had to cut his minutes down to almost nothing. After a game against Utah where Hardaway sat out completely, Spoelstra spoke about the need for change. He said, “I get it for Timmy…sometimes you have to make a change.” The team simply cannot play him if he cannot guard or score. Ryan Conwell has taken his spot because he plays with more energy. Clutch Time Is The Test Mitchell shines when the clock runs low and the pressure is high. The Heat as a team struggles in these late-game moments. They shoot just 32.1 percent with under four seconds left on the clock. This is the fifth-worst mark in the league. When the clock gets tight, their three-point percentage drops to a terrible 22.6 percent. Mitchell flips that script with his own shot. He has a 40 percent field goal percentage in late shot clock situations. He is tied for sixth in the league for three-point shooting in those same moments. Yahoo Sports notes that the logic of playing only who is in front of you is faulty, yet Mitchell proves his worth every night. item.description: Credit: Rich Storry-Imagn Images Chris Bell The Miami Dolphins face a tough spot with rookie wide receiver Chris Bell likely missing Sunday’s game against the Indianapolis Colts. Head coach Jeff Hafley said Bell would probably be listed as doubtful due to a knee injury, per Sports Illustrated . This is a setback, but it is not the torn ACL that ended Bell’s college season last year. The pain came during a practice hit on Wednesday, which stopped him from working on Thursday and Friday. Bell’s season has been rough so far, even though he made the team out of training camp. He has played in all eight games but only caught 12 passes for 148 yards, according to Sports Illustrated. The rookie also failed to catch a single ball in three different games, including the loss to Detroit where he was targeted just once. McCord steps in for the injured Malik Willis and needs reliable targets to feel comfortable. If Bell sits out, fifth-round rookie Kevin Coleman Jr. could see more time, per Yahoo Sports . The team already has Caleb Douglas and Malik Washington ahead of Bell in the rotation. Veteran Jalen Tolbert might return to the lineup if Jared Wayne stays out with his own quad issue. Other Key Absences Loom Bell is not the only player dealing with health problems this week. Center Aaron Brewer will miss the game because he is still in concussion protocol, Hafley confirmed. item.title: Andorra goalkeeper banned for 12 matches after Jesus de Miguel’s death following on-pitch collision
item.description: A 12-match ban has been handed to Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono following the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel after an on-field collision between the pair. The Spanish soccer federation’s disciplinary committee imposed the suspension on Friday, 10 days after De Miguel died a day following his clash with Owono. The goalkeeper had received a red card following the incident, and the disciplinary committee said Owono used “excessive force” in the collision. The incident took place near the end of the match in Tenerife on 2 November. De Miguel was chasing a high ball in midfield when he was struck in the chest by Owono, who had rushed far outside his area. The 30-year-old suffered cardiac arrest following the collision. He died the next day. Owono issued a statement through his club expressing his remorse and offering his condolences to De Miguel’s family. Tributes have been paid to Jesus de Miguel following his death (Getty) “These are the most difficult days of my life,” Owono said. “I’m struggling to find the words and finding it very difficult to process anything that has happened. “I feel enormous pain at the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and all the people who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I can’t think of anything other than Jesus and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.” Spanish police opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter. Under Spanish law, deaths from non-natural causes, including accidents, are subject to judicial investigation, though prosecutors have said that criminal proceedings are unlikely. On Thursday, Andorra coach Carles Manso said it will be up to Owono to decide when he feels ready to play again. “He is deeply affected by the situation,” Manso said. “We will give him the space to feel completely free to decide whether, and when, he might want to return.” Owono was not selected by Equatorial Guinea for their Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers during the ongoing international break following last week’s collision. Owono has been Equatorial Guinea’s first-choice goalkeeper since he was a teenager and competed with them at the last three Africa Cup of Nations finals.

item.title: Dolphins Roster Crisis Deepens As Uche Steps Up Amid Injury Woes
item.description: Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images The Miami Dolphins are facing a brutal stretch with their depth getting tested hard. After losing to the Detroit Lions, the team announced more key starters are sidelined. Head coach Jeff Hafley confirmed that center Aaron Brewer will not play against the Indianapolis Colts. Brewer remains stuck in the NFL’s concussion protocol and has not practiced once this week, per Heavy.com . Rookie wide receiver Chris Bell is also doubtful for Sunday after missing practice with a knee issue. The Dolphins now sit at 1-7 on the season, and their margin for error has vanished completely. Because Malik Willis and Zach Sieler are already on injured reserve, the roster is thin. Sieler suffered a ruptured biceps on the first play of the last game and is out for the entire season. Willis will miss four weeks with a core muscle injury. Now Brewer and Bell add to the list of missing pieces. The team must find a way to win with a backup center and a shaky receiving corps against a struggling Colts squad. Leadership Shifts as Veterans Step In When captains get hurt, someone else has to speak up for the group. Edge rusher Josh Uche has been named a new captain to fill the void left by Willis and Sieler. Uche, a seven-year veteran and Miami native, has been mentoring younger players all season. He accepted the role with a humble attitude, focusing on the upcoming game rather than the honor itself. “It’s still a dream just playing football, man,” Uche said at his locker Wednesday, per the Sun Sentinel . Coach Hafley opened the captaincy to other players who earned the spot, and the team agreed unanimously. Hafley noted that it was good to see players give opportunities to others. Uche plans to keep his head down and do the work needed for the next matchup. “They let me know the news and it’s a plus, but we’re on to the Colts,” Uche said. Lineup Changes and Practice Reports Andrew Meyer is expected to start at center in place of the injured Brewer. Meyer has worked closely with backup quarterback Kyle McCord during practice sessions, which should help their chemistry. Hafley called it a “positive” that the two have already led the scout team together. This familiarity might be the only good news for the offense as they prepare to face the Colts. The rookie Bell will not practice on Friday and remains doubtful, though Hafley did not rule him out completely. Bell’s knee issue is not related to his previous ACL tear from college, so it is not a long-term setback. He appeared in every game this season before this injury hit. The Dolphins have lost their starting quarterback, center, and a top defensive lineman in a short span. This combination of losses will impact both sides of the ball significantly. The team must rely on depth players to step up immediately if they want to avoid another loss. On Sunday, Nov. 15, at 1 p.m. ET at Lucas Oil Stadium, the Dolphins will take on the Indianapolis Colts.

item.description: James Rowson, seen here from his time with the Marlins as their bench coach, watches batting practice before a game against the Philadelphia Phillies, Saturday, April 16, 2022, in Miami. (Lynne Sladky/Associated Press) There's a new offensive coordinator in town, and this one isn't working out of Levi's Stadium. The San Francisco Giants hired James Rowson to be the franchise's first offensive coordinator, which means he'll be a hitting coach while also dealing with baserunning and other facets of the offense starting in 2027. Rowson, 50, asked for the title during the interview process, president of baseball operations Buster Posey explained. The Giants are likely to also hire a hitting coach to replace Hunter Mense, who left for the Kansas City Royals. The new coaches will work alongside assistant hitting coach Oscar Bernard, a holdover. For Rowson, the title of offensive coordinator speaks to his philosophy, that like football, there should be a coach who can tie all the facets of the offensive game together. "In the NFL they have running backs coaches, they have wide receiver coaches, they have individual coaches for areas, but at the end of the day, they have an offensive coordinator who's trying to put all that together," Rowson said on Friday. "One who's trying to figure out what's the best way for us to go out there and score as a club." This isn't a new concept in baseball. The Milwaukee Brewers, Royals and Texas Rangers are among the teams with offensive coordinators. "Offense is to score runs to win the game," Rowson said. "It's not about the individual and him getting a hit. It's about whether or not he touches home plate and scores a run." That means Rowson will get in on coaching baserunning. There has been a shift there already, with Taira Uematsu replacing Shane Robinson as the first-base coach. Every year, the Giants proclaim a push to create more runs on the bases with a focus on stealing bags and improved decision-making. But the Giants were hapless at times on the bases in 2026. The recorded minus-5.6 baserunning runs above average, ranking them the fourth-worst team in baseball at creating runs on the bases, according to FanGraphs. "Just being the aggressor," Posey said at the GM meetings in Las Vegas. "Even though I say it to them – there's not going to be repercussions if we get thrown out - there's still a hesitancy there." item.description: Credit: Straight Shooter Stephen A. Smith entered the White House to interview Donald Trump as a podcast host, and he left feeling presidential. The once-growing belief that the ESPN host will eventually run for president has faded in the last year or so. Partly because Smith has insisted he will not give up his highly lucrative media gigs, and partly because he’s built a political platform without being transparent about where he stands on many issues. To Smith’s credit, his political platform landed him at the White House twice in the last month. After joining Bill Maher and Kid Rock for a dinner with Trump at the White House several weeks ago, Smith returned this week to interview the president for his YouTube show . And while reflecting on the interview during a segment with Skip Bayless on his SiriusXM Radio show Friday afternoon, Smith admitted his latest visit to the White House has him feeling like he belongs there. “Once I was leaving, I don’t even know if I should admit this on the air, but it’s true. I kind of felt like I could be here, like I could do this,” Smith told Bayless. As he left the White House, reporters closed in on Smith to take pictures and get comments before he was ushered over to a designated stakeout position to answer questions . And in that moment, Smith really began to feel in his element. “I felt kinda presidential. I really really did. I was like, this is kinda cool,” Smith said on his Mad Dog Sports Radio show. “I wasn’t scared to answer any questions. And then Trump’s staff came running out to get me away from there. I’m thinking they didn’t want me talking until the interview came out. I come to find out once I had left, they were trying to get me out of there so I didn’t have to talk to the media cause they thought I minded. item.title: Germany sink sorry Serbia to set up crunch Netherlands clash
item.description: Germany coach Jurgen Klopp watched on as his side won 3-1 in Belgrade on Friday (Pedja Milosavljevic) Germany cruised to a 3-1 win against Serbia in Belgrade in the Nations League on Friday, setting up a crunch clash with the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday. In teeming rain in an almost empty stadium, the Germans forced Serbia's Srdan Babic into an early own goal with Florian Wirtz and debutant Brajan Gruda also scoring. Babic made up for his blunder with a second-half consolation strike, while Serbia finished with nine men after substitutes Vanja Dragojevic and Andrija Zivkovic were sent off late on. The Netherlands' 7-0 annihilation of Greece in Amsterdam means the Germans will likely need to win on Monday to reach the quarter-finals, unless Serbia beat the Greeks away from home. Germany have now won twice, drawn twice and lost once in five games under coach Jurgen Klopp, who was optimistic the side were beginning to take shape under his tutelage. "We played a truly fantastic game. I think we need to get a bit more used to the fact that we're genuinely good -- and capable of being very, very good," Klopp told RTL. "Our counter-pressing was superb, and the intensity was top-notch. So, from my point of view, it was a really, really good game. "We wanted to qualify for that 'final' in Berlin, and now we have... It's great. We're looking forward to it, and we have a wealth of options to choose from." Serbia are guaranteed to finish bottom of the group after a fifth loss in a row. "It was very difficult for Serbia, who certainly aren't at their best right now," Klopp said. "And yet, in games like this, you can easily end up hurting yourself - but we didn't." - Schoolchildren and German fans only - With Serbia's fans banned by UEFA due to racist and discriminatory behaviour earlier in the competition, the teams took to the field with the cavernous Rajko Mitic Stadium almost empty. Just 5,000 schoolchildren -- and 200 travelling Germany fans -- were allowed to attend. Germany shrugged off the wet and wild conditions in the Serbian capital by taking the lead after just two minutes. Kai Havertz, starting up front ahead of the recalled Niclas Fuellkrug, headed a corner centrally which took a deflection off Babic and trickled over the line. Havertz was again instrumental when Germany added a second on 14 minutes. The Arsenal forward broke through the Serbian defence and while his close-range shot was well saved, the ball fell to his one-time Bayer Leverkusen teammate Wirtz, who guided it over the line. Gruda notched Germany's third just after the break with a spectacular solo effort on debut. The RB Leipzig winger collected the ball near halfway and marched upfield before skimming a low shot into the corner. Babic pulled one back for Serbia just before the hour mark, the defender perfectly placed to tap in when Marc-Andre ter Stegen palmed a Nemanja Gudelj shot directly at his feet.
